summary:
ONE-WAY RADIO is an interactive five-sol Mars mission command trainer designed to help young learners understand the challenges of communicating across interplanetary distances.
Players take the role of an Earth-based Mission Commander responsible for guiding a four-person crew at a remote Mars outpost. With one-way communication delays ranging from 3 to 22 minutes, commands cannot produce instant results. Players must interpret delayed telemetry, manage oxygen, water, food and electrical energy, prioritise risks, and make decisions with incomplete information.
The simulation introduces three command slots per transmission window, a planned communications blackout, standing orders and four layers of crew autonomy. Players discover that successful mission leadership requires more than issuing instructions: it requires trust, preparation and allowing crew members to exercise sound judgement when Earth cannot respond in time.
By turning communication latency into a playable decision-making experience, ONE-WAY RADIO makes complex space exploration concepts accessible while developing systems thinking, resource management, problem-solving and leadership skills.
details:
ONE-WAY RADIO: The Delay Is the Game

ONE-WAY RADIO is an interactive five-sol Mars mission command trainer designed to introduce young learners to the challenges of human space exploration. Players take the role of an Earth-based Mission Commander guiding a four-person crew at a remote Mars outpost.

The simulation turns communication delay into its central gameplay mechanic. Depending on the mission sol, a command takes 3–22 minutes to reach Mars, and telemetry arrives with a delay. Players must interpret incomplete or outdated information, prioritise emergencies, and manage oxygen, water, food, stored electrical energy, and power generation. Each transmission window allows only three command slots. A planned communications blackout on Sol 3 requires the crew to continue operating without new instructions from Earth.

The project’s distinctive feature is its crew-autonomy system. Through The Gap, Discretion Clauses, Rogue Events, and Unofficial Acts, crew members can respond to situations independently when direct communication is unavailable. This makes trust, preparation, and sound judgement important parts of mission leadership not simply issuing commands.

ONE-WAY RADIO aims to make complex spaceflight concepts accessible while developing systems thinking, resource management, problem-solving, decision-making, and leadership skills. Its intended impact is to help young learners understand why communication delays, limited resources, and crew autonomy matter in deep-space exploration.

The project was developed as a web-based application using React, TypeScript, and Vite, with AI-assisted development tools. The team considered the target age group, scientific plausibility, mission safety, clarity of learning objectives, accessibility, responsive design, and performance on typical school computers. Its creative approach is to make the communication delay itself not a conventional score or action mechanic the central challenge of the experience.
